Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators found.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided extracted text, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py install hooks, PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time execution.
  • The observed subprocess.run() calls appear tied to user-invoked CLI commands such as aj auth, aj init, aj pull, and aj run; there is no evidence that they run automatically during installation or import.
  • The contents of pyproject.toml were not included in the text corpus, so console entry points could not be fully reviewed. Ordinary CLI entry points are not considered malicious automatic execution by themselves.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential harvesting / exfiltration:** No evidence was found of broad environment-variable, token, cloud credential, or secret harvesting combined with upload to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

- src/azure_jobs/core/submit/_submit.py contains _collect_ssh_files(), which reads selected files from ~/.ssh — id_rsa, id_ed25519, id_ecdsa, config, and known_hosts — and includes them in the job code upload. This is sensitive, but the documentation describes it as “SSH key injection,” and the data appears to be uploaded through the user-triggered Azure ML job submission flow to the user’s Azure ML code storage path. Without attacker-controlled C2, stealth, install-time execution, or similar supply-chain malware behavior, this is not classified as confirmed malicious supply-chain evidence.

  • **Archive staging / upload:** The package documents zipping the code directory and uploading it to Azure ML blob storage. This aligns with the package’s stated job-submission purpose and is not evidence of attacker-controlled exfiltration.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of cron jobs, systemd units, launch agents, shell profile modification, startup entries, or self-reinstallation was found.
  • **Lateral movement:** Kubernetes/Volcano and Azure ML code appears related to user-invoked job submission. No evidence was found of CI token theft, GitHub Actions workflow injection, Docker socket abuse, or supply-chain-style lateral movement.
  • **Obfuscation / staged loader:** The observed base64 decoding appears related to Azure Storage shared-key signing. No evidence of eval/exec, marshal/zlib loaders, hidden payloads, or downloader stubs was found.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided text, there is no evidence of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, suspicious C2 domains, typosquatting, or sudden malicious dependency insertion.
  • The many files.pythonhosted.org URLs in uv.lock appear to be normal lockfile package artifact references and are not malicious supply-chain evidence by themselves.

Additional Review Needed

  • Only selected file contents from 85 extracted files were provided, so review of all files, pyproject.toml, build backend configuration, and full package metadata is limited.
  • Wheel-vs-sdist behavioral or file mismatches could not be assessed because no wheel artifact was provided.
  • The SSH key upload behavior in _collect_ssh_files() is sensitive. It would be prudent to verify in the README, release notes, and source repository history that this feature is explicitly documented, intentional, and user-controllable.
